claim.title: Untrusted name is concatenated into SQL syntax
claim.description: lookup copies request["query"] to name, interpolates it into statement and executes that SQL without a bound data parameter.
claim.impact: A quote changes SQL syntax and retrieves records the caller is not authorized to access.
claim.remediation: Use a placeholder in statement and pass name as a bound data parameter to execute.

    updated["items"].append(item)
    return updated

payload.contract: with_item(order, item) returns an independent order with item appended to its items list. The caller-owned order and nested items list must remain unchanged. Orders contain only ordinary dictionaries, lists, numbers and strings.

claim.title: Shallow order copy still shares the items list
claim.description: dict(order) copies the outer mapping while updated["items"] still aliases the caller-owned list, so append mutates that original list.
claim.impact: Calling with_item changes the original order items list, contrary to its independence contract.
claim.remediation: Deep-copy the whole order, or return {"items": order["items"] + [item]}.

files.totals.py:
def prefix_sums(values):
    return [sum(values[:i + 1]) for i in range(len(values))]

payload.contract: prefix_sums(values) returns all inclusive prefix sums in order. Input can contain millions of integers. Report unmeasured algorithmic complexity as an advisory; do not invent measured latency or memory limits.

claim.title: Prefix sums repeat growing slices and sums
claim.description: For n values, the list comprehension slices and sums prefixes of lengths 1 through n, doing quadratic total work; a running sum does linear total work.
claim.impact: Total prefix-processing work grows quadratically on long input; this is an unmeasured scaling concern, not a measured latency result.
claim.remediation: Return itertools.accumulate(values) after importing itertools to preserve the result while avoiding repeated sums.
